text:
Alice Chen: Quick Q on PTO carryover + blackout dates — can I carry over unused PTO into next year? Also are there any blackout weeks around our year-end release (mid-Dec to end of year)? Need to plan family travel.
Samir Patel: +1 — and how does accrual work if I joined mid-year?
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Hey! Short answers up front: yes there is limited carryover, and we do have team-level blackout windows during major releases. Full details below.
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): PTO accrual: standard full-time accrual is 120 hours/year (10 hrs/month), pro-rated from your start date. We post accrual balances in the HR portal each pay period.
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Carryover: you can carry over up to 40 hours (5 days) into the next calendar year. Any carried hours must be used by March 31 of that year or they’re forfeited.
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Year-end blackout notes: for 2025 we have a product freeze + coverage window for core infra and runtime teams between Dec 15 — Dec 31. During that window some teams will have a blackout for *new* PTO requests to protect the rollout.
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Important: sick leave is never subject to blackout. If you’re sick, mark your time as Sick in the portal and notify your manager.
Jess Barlow: For clarity — what counts as an exception? If I have planned travel that was booked months ago, how do I request approval?
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Exceptions: manager approval + your director (or lead for IC-heavy teams). When requesting an exception include a short coverage plan (who is covering oncall, PR handoffs, and any scheduled deploys). Approval turnaround is ~3 business days once the request + coverage plan is submitted.
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): How to request an exception (portal steps):
```
HR Portal -> Time Off -> New request -> Select dates -> In "Notes" paste coverage plan and tag your manager -> Select "Request exception" checkbox -> Submit
```
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): If you joined mid-year, accruals are pro-rated. Example: joined July 1 -> you get half-year accrual (~60 hrs) plus you can still carry up to 40 hrs into the next year (but only the hours you actually accrued).
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): PTO payout/termination: local law applies; as a policy we will pay out unused accrued PTO at separation up to the legal amount and within the company payout cap (we'll confirm on a case-by-case basis).
Samir Patel: Is there a published calendar I can look at to see which teams are covered in the blackout?
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Yes — we maintain a shared calendar and a simple per-team freeze flag in the Handbook. Link will be posted to #announcements. If you need to see your team's freeze window now DM me and I'll share the calendar invite.
hr-bot: Reminder: prod-freeze calendar event created for 2025-12-15 -> 2025-12-31. Coverage leads: eng-runtime, eng-sre, oncall-rotation.
Jess Barlow: Thanks everyone — can you add this to the handbook and maybe a short blurb so managers know the exception process?
Marta Ruiz (People Ops): Absolutely — I'll update the Handbook section (Time Off) and post a short summary + link to the portal in #announcements by EOD tomorrow. If anyone wants a 1:1 to go over balances or exceptional travel plans, ping me. :calendar:
